title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Deployment Guide, Reference Architectures, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade and Rollback
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s recommended practices for private deployments (VPC and on-prem), including reference architectures, on‑prem packaging guidance, day‑2 operational procedures, and detailed upgrade & rollback playbooks. It is intended for platform engineers, solutions architects, and customer success engineers supporting production private deployments.

Overview and audience:
- Purpose: Provide a single, operationally actionable reference for deploying, operating, upgrading and troubleshooting Redwood Private in customer VPCs and air-gapped on‑prem environments.
- Audience: Eng‑private‑deployments engineering, SRE, customer success, and partner implementation teams.

Contents:
1) High level reference architectures
2) Packaging and distribution (on‑prem)
3) VPC deployment checklist and network requirements
4) Day‑2 operations: monitoring, backups, scaling, and incident flow
5) Upgrade and rollback procedures (canary and full upgrades)
6) Customer requirements matrix and packaging checklist
7) Appendix: common commands, config snippets, and troubleshooting tips

1) Reference architectures (high level)
This section describes three supported reference architectures. Pick the one matching the customer requirements for isolation, latency, and operational model.

A. Small‑scale VPC (development / PoC)
- Single Kubernetes cluster (K8s 1.27+ recommended) in customer-managed VPC (EKS/GKE/AKS).
- Dedicated namespace: redwood-private.
- Node pool(s): 1 control plane node pool (m-type), 1 GPU pool (g-type) for inference.
- Minimum: 3 m-type nodes for control plane components (ha for control plane services), 1 GPU node for lightweight PoC.
- Ingress: ALB / NLB with TLS termination managed by customer.
- Data plane: S3-compatible object store (minio or cloud S3) for model artifacts; EFS / PV for persistent data if needed.

B. Production VPC (multi‑AZ, high availability)
- Multi-AZ K8s cluster with dedicated GPU autoscaling groups and control-plane redundancy.
- Recommended sizing: N GPU nodes per expected RPS (see performance guide in benchmarking-and-perf-suite). Typical starting point: 4 x A10/RTX6000-equivalent GPUs for small production; scale from there.
- Internal services behind private ALB/NLB with route53 internal records.
- Private control plane (Redwood components) deployed to a management namespace; customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
- Cross-account role based access for Redwood control plane (when Redwood provides management plane connectivity).

C. Air‑gapped on‑prem (customer data center)
- Distribution: packaged Helm chart + OCI image bundle (see Packaging section).
- On‑prem variant ships with optional offline model bundle (tar.gz of model artifacts) and an operators guide for installing images into local registry.
- Network: minimal outbound URLs required for license checks and optional telemetry; these can be stubbed in fully air-gapped deployments.
- Storage: Ceph/Rook, NFS, or direct-attached NVMe for model cache.
- Hardware: recommended GPU list and driver versions provided in appendix.

2) On‑prem packaging and distribution
Goals: reproducible, auditable, and installable in environments with limited network egress.

Packaging model:
- Release artifacts: 
  - Helm charts (versioned semver).
  - OCI images for all components (control-plane, runtime, sidecars).
  - Optional offline model bundles (SHA256 signed).
  - Installation tarball containing scripts, manifests, and operator-runbook.

Distribution options:
- Online install: Helm repo + Docker/OCI registry access.
- Air‑gapped install: provide OCI bundle (.tar) and model bundle (.tar.gz) with installation instructions to load into local registry.

On‑prem installation checklist (operator-runbook style):
1. Pre-flight: verify kernel, cuda drivers, nvidia-container-runtime, and k8s version.
2. Provision local registry and ensure credentials stored in sealed secret format.
3. Load OCI bundle into local registry: 
   - docker load && docker push to local registry OR use registry import tool.
4. Apply CRDs and Helm chart with values.yaml tuned for local storage paths and nodeSelectors.
5. Validate: run smoke test (see CLI smoke-test below).

Packaging security notes:
- All bundles signed with Redwood GPG and SHA256 sums. Validate signatures before install.
- Provide air‑gap customer a manifest of checksums and a signature verification script.

3) VPC deployment checklist and network requirements
Networking requirements (minimum):
- Internal DNS entries for control-plane services (api.internal.redwood.local).
- Ports: 443 (ingress), 6379 (optional redis for cache), 9000 (internal admin UI, configurable), 8000-8100 (runtime gRPC/HTTP endpoint ranges).
- Storage: S3-compatible endpoint or cloud S3 with bucket policy for model artifacts.
- IAM: service role for Redwood control-plane to access S3 and KMS.

Deployment checklist (pre‑deploy):
- Confirm K8s cluster version and node types.
- Confirm GPU drivers and monitoring agent (nvidia-dcgm).
- Provision S3 bucket and KMS key; exchange ARNs with Redwood implementation engineer.
- Configure VPC routing for private subnets and NAT for optional egress.
- Prepare TLS certificates or ACME integration for ingress.
- Set up logging / metrics endpoints (Prometheus, Loki, Grafana or customer equivalents).

4) Day‑2 operations (monitoring, backups, scaling, incident flow)
Monitoring and metrics:
- Key metrics to track (minimum):
  - Inference latency p50/p90/p99 per model & route (ms).
  - Token throughput (tokens/s) and request RPS.
  - GPU utilization per node (GPU% / memory used).
  - KV cache hit rate and model load times.
  - Disk usage for model cache and logs.
- Dashboards: provide per‑model and per‑route dashboards; example Grafana panel JSON included in companion repo.

Backups and state:
- Control-plane stateless where possible; persistent data: model artifact registry pointer, RBAC configs, and license secrets.
- Backup schedule: daily exported snapshots of CRDs and configmaps to S3-compatible storage (retention 30d by default).
- Restore procedure: documented in runbooks (section: restore-control-plane).

Scaling and performance:
- Horizontal autoscaling: KEDA/HPA on inference frontends based on request queue depth / GPU utilization.
- Batching config: default batch window 8–20ms; tune per latency SLO.
- Cache priming: during scale-up events warm popular model prefixes using a priming job.

Operational play: incident triage flow (summary)
1. Alert triggers: p99 latency > SLO, GPU OOMs, <1 healthy replica for runtime.
2. Triage steps: fetch logs, check node GPU health, confirm model pod readiness, inspect KV cache hit rates.
3. Escalation: page oncall SRE team and include runbook link + recent scaling events.
4. Recovery actions: roll forward to previous model variant, scale up GPU pool, or disable routing to impacted AZ/region.

5) Upgrade and rollback procedures
Principles:
- Minimize inference downtime and preserve model state where possible.
- Prefer canary upgrades with progressive traffic ramp to detect regressions.
- Keep deterministic rollback path tested on staging before production.

Upgrade types:
- Control-plane patch (minor config changes) — low risk, can be performed with Helm rollout.
- Runtime binary or model-serving major upgrade — medium risk, requires canary and performance validation.
- Model artifact update (weights change) — higher risk for quality regressions; always run evals and smoke tests.

Canary upgrade procedure (recommended):
1. Prepare release: build OCI images and update Helm chart version.
2. Deploy to staging cluster and run full smoke + perf tests.
3. Canary deploy in production namespace: create new Deployment with label canary=true and scale to 1–2 pods.
4. Route small percentage of traffic (1–5%) to canary using service mesh (istio/contour) or traffic-splitting mechanism.
5. Monitor key metrics for 30–60 minutes: latency p99, error rate, GPU OOMs, model correctness (sampled prompts).
6. If stable, increment traffic 25/50/100% over predefined intervals.
7. If regression detected, execute rollback procedure below.

Rollback (fast) procedure:
- For Helm-managed control-plane: helm rollback <release> <revision> and verify pod readiness.
- For canary runtime/model regressions: route all traffic away from canary and scale down canary pods; redeploy previous image tag if traffic-splitting not sufficient.
- For catastrophic failures: apply emergency stop to routing layer (route traffic to Redwood-hosted fallback or disabled routes).

Post‑mortem and verification:
- After any upgrade/rollback, collect perf traces and do a root cause analysis; record findings in incident-review and update test suite.

6) Customer requirements library (operator checklist matrix)
This section is a copy‑friendly checklist to capture customer constraints during scoping. Provide to customer success / SEs when scoping Private engagement.

Minimum required customer information:
- Kubernetes version and distribution
- Number and type of GPU nodes (model + count)
- Network topology (VPC peering, private subnets, NAT)
- Egress policy and air-gap constraints
- Storage choices (S3, on-prem object store, NFS)
- Auth/Z: preferred KMS, OIDC provider, and service account policy
- Compliance requirements (e.g., PCI, HIPAA, FedRAMP)

Operational preferences (optional):
- Backup retention (default 30d)
- Alerting thresholds (p99 latency SLO, error budget)
- Maintenance windows and preferred upgrade cadence

7) Appendix: common commands, config snippets, and troubleshooting
Smoke test (CLI):
- kubectl -n redwood-private run smoke-test --rm --image=busybox -- /bin/sh -c "curl -sSfS https://local-runtime:8000/healthz || exit 1"
Helm install example values.yaml snippet:
- values.yaml sample:
  replicaCount: 3
  runtime:
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1
    nodeSelector:
      accelerator: nvidia
  storage:
    modelBucket: "s3://redwood-models-prod"
  telemetry:
    enabled: true

Model bundle verification (sha check):
- sha256sum model-v1.tar.gz && gpg --verify model-v1.tar.gz.sig model-v1.tar.gz

Common troubleshooting checklist:
- GPU OOMs: check model batch size and reduce concurrency; inspect runtime logs for cuda_mem errors.
- Slow cold starts: verify model cache warmers are running and check network throughput to model store.
- KV cache corruption: restart runtime with cache-clear flag and monitor hit rate.

Ownership and escalation paths:
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments team.
- Oncall escalation: eng-sre -> eng-platform -> eng-serving-runtime.
- Customer support handoff: customer-success handles first-line and escalates to eng-private-deployments when implementation-level changes are required.
